clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old sexually active homosexual male presented to the ED with five days of acute painless progressive bilateral vision loss. Initial examination revealed visual acuity of 20/600 bilaterally with bilateral vitritis, white tufts, and globular white opacities on fundoscopy consistent with posterior uveitis. The patient had recent alopecia suggestive of secondary syphilis. Workup revealed positive CSF VDRL (1:2) with pleocytosis (WBC 33 cells/μL), elevated protein (44 mg/dL), and low glucose (53 mg/dL), confirming neurosyphilis. The patient was found to be HIV-positive (CD4 1347 cells/μL, viral load 52,900 c/mL), which increases susceptibility to neurosyphilis and ocular manifestations. IV penicillin G was initiated for a 14-day course. The constellation of acute bilateral posterior uveitis with characteristic fundoscopic findings, positive CSF VDRL, CSF pleocytosis with elevated protein and low glucose, recent alopecia, and HIV co-infection established the diagnosis of syphilitic posterior uveitis with CNS involvement.
